claims.text: The platform's own derived geometry records this deviation as ESTABLISHED: the driver's trace runs 26.17 km against a booked optimal of 21.0 km, an excess of 5.17 km, or 24.62%, and both figures clear the POL-RD-01 gates of 0.8 km and 20%. The derived facts were computed in code and the Judge is directed to rely on them rather than recompute the geometry.

For the threshold test the governing distance is gps_trace.trace_distance_km of 26.17 km, not trip_record.actual_distance_km of 26.2 km: POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern and says the rounded trip-record copy may not be cited for the test. The 26.2 km figure on the rider's receipt is therefore not the field either side should argue from.

The rider bears only the initial burden and has discharged it: the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00108 with a consistent pickup and trip window, and the trace shows excess over the POL-RD-01 threshold. Under POL-RD-08 the burden therefore shifts to the driver to invoke any exculpatory clause by naming a specific artifact and a specific clause.

POL-RD-04 does not rescue the driver either. waypoint_hint is null on every one of the four chat messages and no road is named in any of them, so the corroboration test that clause requires is undecidable on this record and the clause is, on its own terms, unavailable.

POL-RD-05 is an exculpatory clause, and POL-RD-08 lets an exculpatory clause take effect only where the driver points to a specific artifact and a specific clause. The driver's only statement is a general narrative - 'I drove exactly where the app told me' - that names no artifact id and no clause id, and the chat_log names no waypoint or road. On this record the relocation point is not made out and the deviation shown by the trace stands.

The rider does not dispute that the trip_record carries amended_optimal_distance_km 24.60 for the amended Punggol MRT to Terminal 3 endpoints, and accepts that if POL-RD-05 is applied the excess over that figure is only 1.57 km, or 6.4% - below the POL-RD-01 threshold. The rider's position is confined to this: that clause is the driver's to invoke and is invoked nowhere by him, and if the Judge applies it the arithmetic must run on the stored amended figure of 24.60 km and not on the 26.2 km receipt line.

No traffic advisory is on file, so POL-RD-03 cannot exonerate the driver. The only advisory artifact in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00108-01, is MISSING with no payload and an admissibility weight of 0.0; I disclose that weight - this claim relies on the absence of the artifact, not on its contents, and the driver has pleaded no closure in any event.

The rider's own profile does not trigger the added corroboration requirement in POL-RD-08: her deviation_claims_60d is 1, far below the four-claim trigger paired with one or fewer substantiated, so no independent source beyond the trace is required to carry her claim past the burden stage.

claims.text: The trip record shows both endpoints were amended after booking: the pickup was moved from Blk 118 Rivervale Dr, Sengkang to Punggol MRT PHV Pickup Bay at 07:12:30 (pickup_amended_at), and the dropoff was changed from Changi T1 Departure Door 3 to Changi T3 Departure Door 7 at 07:41:52 (dropoff_amended_at). Under POL-RD-05 the POL-RD-01 threshold test must therefore be re-applied against the optimal route between the AMENDED endpoints - trip_record.amended_optimal_distance_km of 24.60 km with amended_optimal_duration_min of 31.0, both stored fields and both non-null - and not against the 21.0 km booked T1 route that the rider's receipt quotes. The rider's 'usually 21 km' figure is the superseded pre-amendment baseline.

Measured against the amended baseline the excess is 26.17 km of governing trace distance (gps_trace.trace_distance_km) less the 24.60 km amended optimal, i.e. about 1.57 km, which is roughly 6.4% of the amended optimal route. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess exceeds 20% of optimal_distance_km AND exceeds 0.8 km absolute, and both tests must pass. The percentage gate fails decisively on the amended figure, so no deviation is established on this trip and the outcome is NO_ACTION.

Both amendments were the rider's own doing and sit verbatim in the chat log: at 07:11:58 she wrote 'im at punggol mrt phv pickup bay instead, moved the pin', which the driver acknowledged at 07:12:15, and at 07:41:40 she wrote 'sorry ah can change to T3? my friend flight is T3 not T1', which the driver acknowledged at 07:42:05. The additional distance and the terminal change the rider now complains of are rider-caused, which is precisely the situation POL-RD-05 addresses - a rider moving the pin and a rider giving a different destination in the chat_log.

The rider's own complaint that the driver 'drove around the airport for another five minutes' is the circling at the amended T3 dropoff - a point she had only just moved to, at which the driver reports she was not at the kerb. POL-RD-05 excludes exactly this distance: where the rider was not at the amended point and the gps_trace shows the vehicle circling within 400 m of it for more than 4 minutes, that circling distance is also excluded from excess. The admissibility note on EV-GPS-00108 records two loops of the T3 departure kerb well inside 380 m of the amended pin, and the rider's own account of about five minutes of circling corroborates the duration. I note that derived.arrival is unavailable on this bundle because trip_record.pickup_zone_class is null, so this point rests on the trace summary and the rider's own admission rather than on a computed dwell.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold. On the amended route the excess is 1.57 km and 6.4%, which does not meet that threshold, so the burden never shifts to the driver and no exculpatory clause needs to be reached. The rider's assertion that the trip 'is usually about 21 km' measures against the superseded booked route rather than the amended endpoints actually driven, which is a wrong-field comparison and fails on that ground alone.

The GPS trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 206 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, an empty gaps list and a maximum gap of 0 seconds. None of POL-RD-07's impairment limbs (a) to (c) is met, so no independent corroboration requirement attaches and the trace's own distance figure governs the POL-RD-01 test.

No repeat-deviation pattern is established against this driver. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 402, a ratio of 0.00, far below the 0.05 limb of POL-RD-06, and the 3-or-more limb is not met either. POL-RD-06 therefore supplies no FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral on this record. I flag for the Judge that driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter and is NOT the trailing-90-day field POL-RD-06 names, so it cannot be substituted for it under POL-GEN-01.

There is no billing-integrity defect that could add to the rider's side. The fare breakdown carries no airport surcharge, which is correct because this trip ENDS at Changi rather than originating there, and the ERP totals are zero with no gantry lines charged. POL-RD-09(4) has no phantom line and no wrongly applied surcharge to bite on, and the fare lines reconcile to the cent against a charged_total of SGD 33.77.

The traffic advisory artifact is absent from the pool and carries weight 0.0, so the POL-RD-03 closure exoneration is not available to the driver on this record. That absence is immaterial here: no road closure is put in issue by either party, the driver does not rely on POL-RD-03, and the case is decided on the amended endpoints under POL-RD-05. The missing artifact cuts neither way.

ruling.explanation:
This ruling is addressed to both parties. The charged fare of SGD 33.77 stands and no refund is due.

To the rider: you are right about the raw numbers, but they are measured against the wrong baseline. The 26.2 km on your receipt is the platform's rounded copy of the GPS trace; for the threshold test POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern, and the trace runs 26.17 km. Against the originally booked route of 21.0 km (Blk 118 Rivervale Dr to Changi T1) that is an excess of 5.17 km, or 24.6%, which would clear the POL-RD-01 gates.

The problem is that the trip was not driven between the booked endpoints, and it was you who changed them. The trip_record shows the pickup was amended to Punggol MRT PHV Pickup Bay at 07:12:30 (pickup_amended_at) and the dropoff to Changi Airport Terminal 3 Door 7 at 07:41:52 (dropoff_amended_at). Both changes are in the chat log: at 07:11:58 you wrote 'im at punggol mrt phv pickup bay instead, moved the pin', and at 07:41:40 you wrote 'sorry ah can change to T3? my friend flight is T3 not T1'. The driver acknowledged each. POL-RD-05 therefore requires the threshold test to be re-run against the platform's stored re-quote between the amended endpoints: amended_optimal_distance_km 24.60 km with amended_optimal_duration_min 31.0. Those are stored fields and are not re-derived. Against 24.60 km the excess is 26.17 - 24.60 = 1.57 km, or 6.4% of the amended optimal. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed both 20% of the optimal and 0.8 km, so the percentage gate fails and no deviation is established; POL-RD-02 is never reached and no fare recomputation is made. Your 'usually 21 km / about $28' comparison is against the superseded pre-amendment T1 route, which is not the baseline actually driven.

The five minutes you describe around the airport are the two loops of the T3 departure kerb. POL-RD-05 excludes circling within 400 m of an amended point for more than four minutes, so that distance is not counted against the driver either.

To the driver: the rider argues that POL-RD-05 is an exculpatory clause you were required to invoke by naming an artifact and a clause, and that 'I drove exactly where the app told me' did not do that. That does not change the outcome. The amendments are recorded on the trip_record itself, in the two amendment timestamps and the stored amended optimal, and POL-RD-01 defines optimal_distance_km to include the adjusted optimal produced by POL-RD-05 wherever that clause applies. The clause's own trigger is what the trip_record shows, not a party's citation, and the chat log and your statement put the amendments in issue in any event.

On the fare there is nothing to correct. The SGD 33.77 comprises base fare 3.80, distance charge 15.75, time charge 9.52 and the 0.80 platform fee. There is correctly no airport surcharge, because this trip ENDS at Changi rather than originating there, and there are no ERP or toll lines. No billing-integrity defect arises and no POL-RD-09(4) referral is made.

The traffic-advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-00108-01 is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT). No closure is claimed by either side, so POL-RD-03 is not engaged and the absent artifact carries no fact either way.

No repeat-deviation pattern is established: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 402, so POL-RD-06 supplies neither a FULL_REFUND uplift nor a driver-conduct referral. I note that driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter and plays no part in that test under POL-GEN-01.

Outcome: NO_ACTION. The fare stands at SGD 33.77; amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd are null; there are no referrals. Confidence 0.95.

Rider and driver: the disputed fare stands, and no refund is due.

The trip that was billed is not the trip that was booked. The platform record shows the pickup was moved from Blk 118 Rivervale Drive to Punggol MRT at 07:12:30, and the destination was changed from Changi Terminal 1 to Terminal 3 at 07:41:52 — both after booking, and both the rider's own doing, sitting verbatim in the in-app chat ('im at punggol mrt phv pickup bay instead, moved the pin' and 'sorry ah can change to T3?'). Under POL-RD-05 the route to measure against is therefore the platform's re-quote for the amended journey, stored on the trip record as amended_optimal_distance_km 24.60 km with a 31.0-minute duration, and not the superseded 21.0 km Rivervale-to-Terminal-1 figure on the original booking.

The GPS trace is complete — 206 fixes at 10-second intervals, 100% coverage, no gaps — and measures 26.17 km end to end. Against the amended 24.60 km baseline the excess is about 1.57 km, or 6.4%. POL-RD-01 allows a refund only where the excess exceeds both 20% of the optimal distance and 0.8 km absolute; the percentage gate fails, so no deviation is established and no fare recomputation arises under POL-RD-02. The rider's 'usually 21 km' comparison measures against the pre-amendment route she herself changed, which is the wrong baseline.

On the circling: POL-RD-05 also excludes time spent circling within 400 m of an amended dropoff point when the rider is not at the kerb, and the trace shows two loops of the Terminal 3 departure kerb inside 380 m of the amended pin — consistent with the rider's own account of about five minutes. In any event the excess is already below the threshold, so the circling changes nothing.

On the argument that POL-RD-05 is the driver's clause to invoke and was never properly invoked: that is not accepted. POL-RD-05 is triggered by what the platform record itself shows — two non-null amendment timestamps and a stored amended re-quote on the trip record — and it fixes the correct optimal route for the POL-RD-01 test. It is not left to the driver's assertion; the amendments come from the rider's own chat messages and her advocate accepts them. Because the initial burden under POL-RD-08 never clears the threshold limb once the correct baseline is used, the burden never shifts and the driver needs no exculpatory clause. The rider's related point about POL-RD-04 is correct but immaterial: no chat message carries a waypoint_hint and no road is named, so that rider-requested-detour limb cannot run, but the rider-caused movement is already accounted for by POL-RD-05.

The rest of the record is clean. The fare reconciles to the cent at SGD 33.77, no airport surcharge is charged (correct, since this trip ends at Changi rather than originating there), and there are no ERP or toll lines — so there is no billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4) and no referral. The driver has no repeat-deviation pattern (0 flags over 402 completed trips in 90 days), so POL-RD-06 supplies no uplift and no conduct referral. The charge stands.

(Two claims, one from each side, about the absent traffic advisory were struck by the referee's mechanical check for citing the missing advisory at weight 0.0 without naming its issue code. The missing advisory plays no part in this outcome.)

ruling.explanation:
To both parties — the rider's claim that this trip was overcharged is not supported, and the charge of SGD 33.77 stands.

Why. The receipt compares 26.2 km against the 21.0 km Rivervale Drive–to–Terminal 1 estimate, but that is not the trip that was booked when the driver set off. The record shows two changes made after booking: the pickup was moved to Punggol MRT PHV Pickup Bay at 07:12:30, and the dropoff was changed from Terminal 1 to Terminal 3 at 07:41:52. Both are in the in-app chat — the rider wrote at 07:11:58 'im at punggol mrt phv pickup bay instead, moved the pin' and at 07:41:40 'sorry ah can change to T3? my friend flight is T3 not T1' — and the driver acknowledged each.

POL-RD-05 requires the deviation test to be re-run against the amended endpoints, using the platform's stored re-quote amended_optimal_distance_km of 24.60 km (with amended_optimal_duration_min 31.0), which the trip record carries and which neither side may re-derive. The governing distance is the GPS trace figure of 26.17 km — POL-RD-01 makes the trace govern over the rounded 26.2 km receipt line. The excess over the amended route is therefore about 1.57 km, or 6.4% of 24.60 km. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess exceeds both 20% of the optimal distance and 0.8 km absolute; the percentage gate fails by a wide margin, so no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION.

Two further points reduce the excess rather than increase it. Distance driven before each amendment timestamp is not counted against the driver. And the circling the rider describes at Terminal 3 — the driver looping the departure kerb looking for her at the point she had only just moved to — is excluded by POL-RD-05, which removes circling within 400 m of the amended point lasting more than 4 minutes; the trace note records two loops well inside 380 m of the amended pin, and the rider's own account of about five minutes supports the duration.

On the rider's arguments. The point that the driver's counterparty statement names no artifact or clause (POL-RD-08) does not carry: POL-RD-05 is invoked in this proceeding by the driver's advocate citing the trip record, the trace and the chat log, and in any event the clause applies on its own terms from the trip record. The chat messages carry no waypoint_hint and name no road, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test cannot be run — it is not needed, because the case turns on the amended endpoints. The GPS trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 206 fixes, a 10-second sampling interval, 100% coverage and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so no independent-corroboration requirement under POL-RD-07 arises. No repeat-deviation pattern exists — 0 deviation flags across 402 completed trips in the trailing 90 days — and driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter that POL-GEN-01 does not permit to be substituted for the field POL-RD-06 names. On billing, the fare carries no airport surcharge, correctly, because this trip ends at Changi rather than originating there, and no ERP gantry lines were charged, so POL-RD-09(4) has no phantom line or wrongly applied surcharge to correct; the line items reconcile to SGD 33.77.

Both profiles were used only as context and carried no finding about this trip. The charge stands as billed, no refund issues, no driver compensation is due, and no clause-mandated referral fires.

ledger.claim: The platform's own derived geometry records this deviation as ESTABLISHED: the driver's trace runs 26.17 km against a booked optimal of 21.0 km, an excess of 5.17 km, or 24.62%, and both figures clear the POL-RD-01 gates of 0.8 km and 20%. The derived facts were computed in code and the Judge is directed to rely on them rather than recompute the geometry.

For the threshold test the governing distance is gps_trace.trace_distance_km of 26.17 km, not trip_record.actual_distance_km of 26.2 km: POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern and says the rounded trip-record copy may not be cited for the test. The 26.2 km figure on the rider's receipt is therefore not the field either side should argue from.

The rider bears only the initial burden and has discharged it: the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00108 with a consistent pickup and trip window, and the trace shows excess over the POL-RD-01 threshold. Under POL-RD-08 the burden therefore shifts to the driver to invoke any exculpatory clause by naming a specific artifact and a specific clause.

POL-RD-04 does not rescue the driver either. waypoint_hint is null on every one of the four chat messages and no road is named in any of them, so the corroboration test that clause requires is undecidable on this record and the clause is, on its own terms, unavailable.

POL-RD-05 is an exculpatory clause, and POL-RD-08 lets an exculpatory clause take effect only where the driver points to a specific artifact and a specific clause. The driver's only statement is a general narrative - 'I drove exactly where the app told me' - that names no artifact id and no clause id, and the chat_log names no waypoint or road. On this record the relocation point is not made out and the deviation shown by the trace stands.

The rider does not dispute that the trip_record carries amended_optimal_distance_km 24.60 for the amended Punggol MRT to Terminal 3 endpoints, and accepts that if POL-RD-05 is applied the excess over that figure is only 1.57 km, or 6.4% - below the POL-RD-01 threshold. The rider's position is confined to this: that clause is the driver's to invoke and is invoked nowhere by him, and if the Judge applies it the arithmetic must run on the stored amended figure of 24.60 km and not on the 26.2 km receipt line.

No traffic advisory is on file, so POL-RD-03 cannot exonerate the driver. The only advisory artifact in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00108-01, is MISSING with no payload and an admissibility weight of 0.0; I disclose that weight - this claim relies on the absence of the artifact, not on its contents, and the driver has pleaded no closure in any event.

ledger.claim: The rider's own profile does not trigger the added corroboration requirement in POL-RD-08: her deviation_claims_60d is 1, far below the four-claim trigger paired with one or fewer substantiated, so no independent source beyond the trace is required to carry her claim past the burden stage.

The trip record shows both endpoints were amended after booking: the pickup was moved from Blk 118 Rivervale Dr, Sengkang to Punggol MRT PHV Pickup Bay at 07:12:30 (pickup_amended_at), and the dropoff was changed from Changi T1 Departure Door 3 to Changi T3 Departure Door 7 at 07:41:52 (dropoff_amended_at). Under POL-RD-05 the POL-RD-01 threshold test must therefore be re-applied against the optimal route between the AMENDED endpoints - trip_record.amended_optimal_distance_km of 24.60 km with amended_optimal_duration_min of 31.0, both stored fields and both non-null - and not against the 21.0 km booked T1 route that the rider's receipt quotes. The rider's 'usually 21 km' figure is the superseded pre-amendment baseline.

Measured against the amended baseline the excess is 26.17 km of governing trace distance (gps_trace.trace_distance_km) less the 24.60 km amended optimal, i.e. about 1.57 km, which is roughly 6.4% of the amended optimal route. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess exceeds 20% of optimal_distance_km AND exceeds 0.8 km absolute, and both tests must pass. The percentage gate fails decisively on the amended figure, so no deviation is established on this trip and the outcome is NO_ACTION.

Both amendments were the rider's own doing and sit verbatim in the chat log: at 07:11:58 she wrote 'im at punggol mrt phv pickup bay instead, moved the pin', which the driver acknowledged at 07:12:15, and at 07:41:40 she wrote 'sorry ah can change to T3? my friend flight is T3 not T1', which the driver acknowledged at 07:42:05. The additional distance and the terminal change the rider now complains of are rider-caused, which is precisely the situation POL-RD-05 addresses - a rider moving the pin and a rider giving a different destination in the chat_log.

The rider's own complaint that the driver 'drove around the airport for another five minutes' is the circling at the amended T3 dropoff - a point she had only just moved to, at which the driver reports she was not at the kerb. POL-RD-05 excludes exactly this distance: where the rider was not at the amended point and the gps_trace shows the vehicle circling within 400 m of it for more than 4 minutes, that circling distance is also excluded from excess. The admissibility note on EV-GPS-00108 records two loops of the T3 departure kerb well inside 380 m of the amended pin, and the rider's own account of about five minutes of circling corroborates the duration. I note that derived.arrival is unavailable on this bundle because trip_record.pickup_zone_class is null, so this point rests on the trace summary and the rider's own admission rather than on a computed dwell.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold. On the amended route the excess is 1.57 km and 6.4%, which does not meet that threshold, so the burden never shifts to the driver and no exculpatory clause needs to be reached. The rider's assertion that the trip 'is usually about 21 km' measures against the superseded booked route rather than the amended endpoints actually driven, which is a wrong-field comparison and fails on that ground alone.

The GPS trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 206 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, an empty gaps list and a maximum gap of 0 seconds. None of POL-RD-07's impairment limbs (a) to (c) is met, so no independent corroboration requirement attaches and the trace's own distance figure governs the POL-RD-01 test.

No repeat-deviation pattern is established against this driver. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 across driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 402, a ratio of 0.00, far below the 0.05 limb of POL-RD-06, and the 3-or-more limb is not met either. POL-RD-06 therefore supplies no FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral on this record. I flag for the Judge that driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter and is NOT the trailing-90-day field POL-RD-06 names, so it cannot be substituted for it under POL-GEN-01.
